content: The implementation guide toolkit includes a stakeholder mapping guide designed to identify and analyze key stakeholders involved in reproductive health and family planning service delivery. This process is essential for preparing to implement the World Health Organization’s (WHO) Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC) and Selected Practice Recommendations (SPR) guidance into national family planning programs. To begin, it is important to understand the concept of stakeholder mapping. This involves exploring and learning about tools such as the sample stakeholder mapping grid, which can then be customized to complete your own stakeholder mapping process. Potential stakeholders are individuals or organizations with an interest in or influence over the integration and implementation of WHO guidance into national family planning programs. These stakeholders may include leaders within their respective organizations. Their perspectives should inform the country’s strategy for integrating the MEC and SPR into national family planning guidelines. Stakeholder mapping allows the implementation team to understand the perspectives, affiliations, and areas of representation of stakeholders, as well as their interests and contributions to the integration of MEC and SPR into national guidelines. To use this tool effectively, it is important to first define what a stakeholder is and understand the process of stakeholder mapping. This involves identifying key stakeholders, analyzing their roles and perspectives, mapping their relationships to the objectives, and prioritizing the level of engagement required. When identifying stakeholders in reproductive health and family planning service delivery, consider all individuals or groups who may have an interest in the implementation team’s objectives, both now and in the future. However, it may not be practical or necessary to engage with all stakeholders at the same level of intensity throughout the process, as the list of stakeholders and their roles may evolve over time. To map the relationships between objectives and stakeholder roles, consider how each stakeholder can contribute to the successful incorporation of updated MEC and SPR recommendations into national policies. When analyzing stakeholders, consider the following questions: What is their organization’s mission and primary contribution to reproductive health and family planning? What outcomes do they aim to achieve? What motivates their work? What is their capacity to engage in the implementation process? Are they supportive or critical of the family planning guidance or the proposed implementation process? Whenever possible, engage directly with stakeholders to better understand their interests and potential roles in the planning and implementation of WHO MEC and SPR guidance. Prioritizing stakeholder engagement should be informed by this analysis. Stakeholders with a high level of influence should be prioritized for engagement early in the implementation process. While all stakeholders contribute to the implementation of family planning guidance, it is important to determine the appropriate level and phase of engagement for each. The stakeholder mapping process includes identifying key stakeholders, analyzing their roles and perspectives, mapping relationships, and prioritizing engagement. Tools such as the sample stakeholder mapping grid, adapted from resources like Business for Social Responsibility (BSR) and the International Association of Public Participation (IAP2), can guide this process.
